question: How does Paul describe his divine calling and apostolic appointment in the opening verse of Romans?
opt1: A servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God
opt2: A ruler of the synagogue, chosen by the elders to preach the law
opt3: A doctor of the law in Jerusalem, sent to inspect the church in Rome
opt4: A bishop over the Gentile churches, appointed by the twelve apostles
correct: A servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God
explanation: Paul establishes his apostolic credentials as a bondservant set apart for God's redemptive gospel. Romans 1:1 (KJV) - "Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,"

question: According to Romans 1:3-4, regarding Christ's two natures, by what was He declared to be the Son of God with power?
opt1: According to the lineage of Aaron, by the anointing of holy oil
opt2: According to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead
opt3: According to the testimony of John, by baptism in the Jordan
opt4: According to the wisdom of Solomon, by signs and wonders
correct: According to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead
explanation: Christ was born of David's line physically, but His divine Sonship was powerfully manifested by His resurrection. Romans 1:3-4 (KJV) - "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:"

question: What report concerning the church at Rome prompted Paul to thank God through Jesus Christ?
opt1: That they had built a grand sanctuary within the city of Rome
opt2: That they had converted the household of Caesar Nero
opt3: That your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world
opt4: That they had sent great offerings of silver to Jerusalem
correct: That your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world
explanation: The vibrant faith of the Roman believers was celebrated across the entire Mediterranean world. Romans 1:8 (KJV) - "First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world."

question: Why was Paul unashamed of the gospel of Christ, as declared in Romans 1:16?
opt1: Because it was approved by the Roman Senate and philosophers
opt2: Because it granted political freedom to all oppressed nations
opt3: Because it abolished all temporal taxes throughout the empire
opt4: For it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth
correct: For it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth
explanation: The gospel is God's effective dynamic power bringing eternal deliverance to all who trust in Christ. Romans 1:16 (KJV) - "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek."

question: Which Old Testament prophecy from Habakkuk does Paul quote in Romans 1:17 to demonstrate how the just shall live?
opt1: The just shall live by faith
opt2: The just shall inherit the earth by works
opt3: The righteous shall prosper by keeping the feast days
opt4: The holy shall be preserved by the blood of bulls
correct: The just shall live by faith
explanation: Quoting Habakkuk 2:4, Paul anchors justification by faith firmly in prophetic Scripture. Romans 1:17 (KJV) - "For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith."

question: Against what is the wrath of God revealed from heaven according to Romans 1:18?
opt1: Against those who refuse to pay the annual temple tribute
opt2: Against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness
opt3: Exclusively against pagan nations that possess no written law
opt4: Against those who fail to observe the outward ceremonial washings
correct: Against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness
explanation: Divine wrath is actively unleashed against all human rebellion that suppresses revealed truth. Romans 1:18 (KJV) - "For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;"

question: Why are all human beings declared without excuse regarding knowledge of God's eternal power and Godhead?
opt1: Because every human being has heard the preaching of the apostles
opt2: Because an angel appeared to every tribe and family on earth
opt3: Because the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen in the things that are made
opt4: Because the moral law was carved upon every mountain by fire
correct: Because the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen in the things that are made
explanation: General revelation in nature renders all humanity morally culpable before the Creator. Romans 1:20 (KJV) - "For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:"

question: What tragic devolution occurred when men, professing themselves to be wise, became fools in Romans 1:23?
opt1: They ceased building stone cities and returned to wilderness caves
opt2: They burned all philosophical books in the public squares
opt3: They refused to honor earthly parents or respect civil magistrates
opt4: Changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and beasts, and creeping things
correct: Changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and beasts, and creeping things
explanation: Idolatry perverts true worship by replacing the transcendent Creator with finite, corruptible creatures. Romans 1:23 (KJV) - "And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things."

question: What fundamental spiritual falsehood defines pagan idolatry in Romans 1:25?
opt1: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator
opt2: Who denied that the material universe had any beginning in time
opt3: Who claimed that angels were equal in majesty to the Most High
opt4: Who worshipped the stars and planets while observing the Sabbath
correct: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator
explanation: The root of all sin is exchanging God's truth for a lie and giving ultimate allegiance to creation. Romans 1:25 (KJV) - "Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen."

question: What judicial consequence followed when men did not like to retain God in their knowledge?
opt1: God sent plagues of locusts to devour their harvests
opt2: God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient
opt3: God destroyed their empires by foreign invading armies
opt4: God removed all memory of language from their tongues
correct: God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient
explanation: Divine abandonment to a depraved, reprobate mind is God's righteous judgment upon willful apostasy. Romans 1:28 (KJV) - "And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;"

question: Why is the self-righteous moralist inexcusable when judging another in Romans 2:1?
opt1: Because no man on earth hath authority to rebuke another
opt2: Because civil judges alone are ordained to administer justice
opt3: For wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things
opt4: Because judgment belongeth exclusively to the priests of Levi
correct: For wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things
explanation: The censorious moralist is self-condemned because he practices the very sins he denounces in others. Romans 2:1 (KJV) - "Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things."

question: What is the true divine purpose of God's goodness, forbearance, and longsuffering toward sinners?
opt1: To grant sinners a license to continue in moral rebellion
opt2: To prove that earthly wealth is the sign of divine approval
opt3: To delay final judgment until all nations build temples
opt4: The goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance
correct: The goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance
explanation: God's patient delay in executing judgment is intended to draw sinners to heartfelt repentance. Romans 2:4 (KJV) - "Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?"

question: What universal standard of impartial justice will God apply to every human being at the judgment?
opt1: Who will render to every man according to his deeds
opt2: Who will judge men solely by their ancestral pedigree
opt3: Who will pardon all who possess a physical copy of the Law
opt4: Who will accept animal sacrifices in place of moral righteousness
correct: Who will render to every man according to his deeds
explanation: God's judgment is strictly according to truth, evaluating individual works without favoritism. Romans 2:6 (KJV) - "Who will render to every man according to his deeds:"

question: What foundational principle of divine equity is explicitly stated in Romans 2:11?
opt1: For the seed of Abraham enjoyeth special immunity from wrath
opt2: For there is no respect of persons with God
opt3: For Roman citizenship protecteth from eternal condemnation
opt4: For the wealthy are judged with greater leniency than the poor
correct: For there is no respect of persons with God
explanation: God demonstrates absolute impartiality, judging Jews and Gentiles by the identical righteous standard. Romans 2:11 (KJV) - "For there is no respect of persons with God."

question: Who are justified before God according to the declaration of Romans 2:13?
opt1: The hearers of the law who memorize its precepts
opt2: The teachers of the law who sit in Moses' seat
opt3: The doers of the law shall be justified
opt4: Those who wear broad phylacteries and make long prayers
correct: The doers of the law shall be justified
explanation: Mere possession or hearing of the Law justifies no one; perfect obedience alone satisfies legal righteousness. Romans 2:13 (KJV) - "(For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified."

question: What inward witness proves that Gentiles without the written Law possess God's moral standard?
opt1: Their public statues and monuments erected in civic plazas
opt2: Their ability to read Greek and Latin philosophical treatises
opt3: Their willingness to offer incense at imperial shrines
opt4: Their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts accusing or else excusing one another
correct: Their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts accusing or else excusing one another
explanation: The universal moral conscience confirms that the work of the Law is written upon the human heart. Romans 2:15 (KJV) - "Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)"

question: According to Romans 2:16, who will judge the secrets of men on that final day according to Paul's gospel?
opt1: God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ
opt2: The twelve patriarchs shall judge their respective tribes
opt3: The archangel Michael shall weigh the deeds of all men
opt4: Moses shall stand as the supreme judge of heaven and earth
correct: God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ
explanation: The Father has committed all ultimate judgment to His Son, Jesus Christ, who knows the hidden secrets of hearts. Romans 2:16 (KJV) - "In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel."

question: What grave accusation did the Scriptures bring against hypocritical Jewish teachers in Romans 2:24?
opt1: Ye have neglected to teach the Hebrew tongue to your children
opt2: The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you
opt3: Ye have refused to trade with the merchants of Tyre and Sidon
opt4: Ye have permitted Greek philosophy to corrupt the temple services
correct: The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you
explanation: Religious hypocrisy causes the holy name of God to be mocked and blasphemed among the surrounding Gentiles. Romans 2:24 (KJV) - "For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written."

question: What defines true circumcision in the sight of God according to Romans 2:29?
opt1: Circumcision performed on the eighth day by a priest of Aaron
opt2: Circumcision accompanied by the offering of two turtledoves
opt3: Circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter
opt4: Circumcision recorded in the civic registry of Jerusalem
correct: Circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter
explanation: True spiritual circumcision is an inward work of the Holy Spirit transforming the heart, not an external rite. Romans 2:29 (KJV) - "But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God."

question: From whom does the true inward Jew receive praise according to Romans 2:29?
opt1: From the elders of the Great Sanhedrin
opt2: From the high priest who inspecteth the temple courts
opt3: From the rulers of the synagogue in every city
opt4: Whose praise is not of men, but of God
correct: Whose praise is not of men, but of God
explanation: Genuine faith seeks divine approval rather than the hollow praise of human religious spectators. Romans 2:29 (KJV) - "But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God."

question: What chief advantage and privilege did the Jewish people possess according to Romans 3:2?
opt1: Chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God
opt2: That they were physically exempt from sickness and pestilence
opt3: That they held supreme political authority over all nations
opt4: That their sins were overlooked without any need of repentance
correct: Chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God
explanation: Israel's preeminent blessing was being entrusted with God's written divine revelation (the Old Testament Scriptures). Romans 3:2 (KJV) - "Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God."

question: What emphatic declaration of divine faithfulness does Paul make against human infidelity in Romans 3:4?
opt1: Let the Law be rewritten according to human wisdom
opt2: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar
opt3: Let both God and man be reconciled through golden gifts
opt4: Let the promises to Abraham be cancelled for ever
correct: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar
explanation: God's immutable truth and covenant fidelity remain absolute even when all humanity proves unfaithful. Romans 3:4 (KJV) - "God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged."

question: What universal diagnosis of human depravity does Paul cite from the Psalms in Romans 3:10?
opt1: A small remnant hath kept the covenant perfectly
opt2: Only the rulers of the Gentiles have gone astray
opt3: There is none righteous, no, not one
opt4: The seed of Levi remaineth pure before the Lord
correct: There is none righteous, no, not one
explanation: Drawing from Psalm 14 and 53, Paul demonstrates the comprehensive unrighteousness of all fallen humanity. Romans 3:10 (KJV) - "As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:"

question: What is the universal consequence when the Law speaks to those under it in Romans 3:19?
opt1: That the Jewish nation may be exalted above all kingdoms
opt2: That men may boast in their ceremonial achievements
opt3: That the temple priesthood may collect tithes from all flesh
opt4: That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God
correct: That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God
explanation: The Law functions as a universal silencer of human boasting, exposing all mankind as guilty before God. Romans 3:19 (KJV) - "Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God."

question: Why can no flesh be justified in God's sight by the deeds of the Law in Romans 3:20?
opt1: For by the law is the knowledge of sin
opt2: Because the Law was intended only for angels in heaven
opt3: Because the Law has been completely corrupted by human scribes
opt4: Because Moses never intended anyone to obey its commands
correct: For by the law is the knowledge of sin
explanation: The Law reveals and diagnoses sin, but possesses zero power to justify or impart spiritual life. Romans 3:20 (KJV) - "Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin."

question: How is the righteousness of God without the Law manifested to sinners in Romans 3:21-22?
opt1: Through annual pilgrimages to the temple altar in Jerusalem
opt2: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe
opt3: Through strict ascetic fasting and self-inflicted scourgings
opt4: By offering the blood of unblemished lambs every morning
correct: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe
explanation: God's gift of righteousness is received entirely by faith in Jesus Christ, apart from legal works. Romans 3:21-22 (KJV) - "But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:"

question: What universal condition unites both Jews and Gentiles in Romans 3:23?
opt1: All are entitled to forgiveness through ancestral heritage
opt2: All possess sufficient natural virtue to please the Creator
opt3: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God
opt4: All are destined to enter the kingdom through good works
correct: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God
explanation: Romans 3:23 provides the sweeping scriptural verdict of universal human guilt and moral failure. Romans 3:23 (KJV) - "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;"

question: How does God justify believing sinners according to the glorious declaration of Romans 3:24?
opt1: By taking into account their sincere intentions and prayers
opt2: By weighing their charitable deeds against their transgressions
opt3: Through their obedience to the oral traditions of the elders
opt4: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus
correct: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus
explanation: Justification is an unmerited, free gift of divine grace grounded in Christ's complete redemptive work. Romans 3:24 (KJV) - "Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:"

question: As what has God set forth Christ Jesus through faith in His blood in Romans 3:25?
opt1: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood
opt2: An earthly monarch to drive out the Roman garrisons
opt3: A second Moses to deliver a more rigorous moral law
opt4: An angelic messenger sent to renovate the temple veil
correct: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood
explanation: Christ is the mercy seat and atoning sacrifice (propitiation) who satisfies divine justice through His blood. Romans 3:25 (KJV) - "Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;"

question: What definitive theological conclusion does Paul establish in Romans 3:28?
opt1: That faith and ceremonial works are equally necessary for salvation
opt2: That a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law
opt3: That circumcision alone ratifieth saving faith before God
opt4: That only those who keep the Sabbath can be declared righteous
correct: That a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law
explanation: The bedrock thesis of Romans: justification is received by faith alone, completely independent of legal works. Romans 3:28 (KJV) - "Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law."

question: What foundational Scripture from Genesis 15:6 does Paul quote regarding Abraham's justification in Romans 4:3?
opt1: Abraham offered Isaac, and by works was he justified
opt2: Abraham kept the statutes of Moses before they were written
opt3: Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness
opt4: Abraham built an altar, and his sacrifice purchased pardon
correct: Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness
explanation: Paul demonstrates that Abraham, the father of the Jewish nation, was justified solely by faith. Romans 4:3 (KJV) - "For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness."

question: How does Paul contrast wages for works with the imputation of righteousness to the believer in Romans 4:4-5?
opt1: Works earn partial grace, which faith subsequently completeth
opt2: God granteth salvation only to those whose works exceed their faults
opt3: Salvation is a loan from God that must be repaid by daily penance
opt4: His faith is counted for righteousness to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly
correct: His faith is counted for righteousness to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly
explanation: Works earn debt, but faith receives the unmerited imputation of righteousness apart from works. Romans 4:4-5 (KJV) - "Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness."

question: Which Psalm of David does Paul cite to prove that God imputes righteousness without works in Romans 4:6-8?
opt1: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin
opt2: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want
opt3: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me
opt4: The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork
correct: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin
explanation: David in Psalm 32 celebrates the non-imputation of sin and the gracious imputation of righteousness. Romans 4:7-8 (KJV) - "Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin."

question: In what state was Abraham when his faith was reckoned for righteousness in Romans 4:10?
opt1: After being circumcised by the priest in Hebron
opt2: Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision
opt3: When he offered the ram in the thicket on Mount Moriah
opt4: After observing the Passover feast with Melchizedek
correct: Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision
explanation: Abraham was justified more than fourteen years prior to his circumcision, proving the rite was not the cause. Romans 4:10 (KJV) - "How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision."

question: What was the true theological role of circumcision in Abraham's life according to Romans 4:11?
opt1: The initial meritorious cause of his eternal salvation
opt2: A guarantee that his descendants would never fall into sin
opt3: A sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised
opt4: A legal covenant binding all Gentiles to the Levitical code
correct: A sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised
explanation: Circumcision was an outward sign and validating seal of the righteousness Abraham already possessed by faith. Romans 4:11 (KJV) - "And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:"

question: Through what means was the promise given to Abraham that he should be heir of the world in Romans 4:13?
opt1: Through his military conquest over the five kings of Canaan
opt2: Through his strict observance of dietary ordinances
opt3: Through his payment of tithes to Melchizedek king of Salem
opt4: Not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith
correct: Not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith
explanation: The universal inheritance promised to Abraham's seed comes entirely through the righteousness of faith. Romans 4:13 (KJV) - "For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith."

question: What effect does the Law produce upon fallen humanity according to Romans 4:15?
opt1: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression
opt2: The Law purifieth the human heart and infuseth eternal love
opt3: The Law granteth power to overcome every fleshly temptation
opt4: The Law abolisheth divine judgment for all who read its words
correct: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression
explanation: The Law provokes and condemns transgressions, working divine wrath rather than salvation. Romans 4:15 (KJV) - "Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression."

question: How does Paul describe God's almighty creative power in Romans 4:17?
opt1: Who weigheth the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance
opt2: Who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were
opt3: Who rideth upon the cherubim and flyeth upon the wings of the wind
opt4: Who planteth the cedars of Lebanon and feedeth the ravens
correct: Who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were
explanation: Abraham believed in the omnipotent God who resurrects the dead and speaks non-existent realities into being. Romans 4:17 (KJV) - "(As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were."

question: How did Abraham respond to God's promise despite his own old age and Sarah's barrenness in Romans 4:20?
opt1: He demanded a physical sign from heaven before believing
opt2: He laughed in cynical despair and returned to Ur of the Chaldees
opt3: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God
opt4: He fasted forty days on Mount Sinai to secure the blessing
correct: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God
explanation: Abraham's unwavering faith gave glory to God by resting fully in His sovereign ability to perform His word. Romans 4:20-21 (KJV) - "He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God; And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform."

question: Why was our Lord Jesus Christ delivered and raised again according to Romans 4:25?
opt1: Delivered to establish an earthly throne, and raised to condemn the Romans
opt2: Delivered to show martyrdom, and raised to become an angelic king
opt3: Delivered to satisfy Roman taxes, and raised to rebuild the temple
opt4: Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification
correct: Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification
explanation: Christ died as an atoning sacrifice for our sins and was raised to secure our complete justification. Romans 4:25 (KJV) - "Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification."

question: What immediate, glorious fruit of justification by faith is proclaimed in Romans 5:1?
opt1: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ
opt2: We are exempt from all physical trials and earthly suffering
opt3: We receive immediate political mastery over earthly rulers
opt4: We are freed from the obligation to love our neighbors
correct: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ
explanation: The hostility caused by sin is eradicated, establishing eternal peace and reconciliation with God. Romans 5:1 (KJV) - "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:"

question: Into what secure spiritual standing do believers have access by faith in Romans 5:2?
opt1: Access into the earthly holy of holies within the Jerusalem temple
opt2: Access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God
opt3: Access to an earthly treasury of silver and gold in Zion
opt4: Access into the royal palace of Caesar as imperial counselors
correct: Access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God
explanation: Believers stand securely in an unshakeable realm of divine favor, exulting in future glory. Romans 5:2 (KJV) - "By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God."

question: What progressive spiritual chain does Christian endurance produce in tribulations according to Romans 5:3-4?
opt1: Tribulation worketh bitterness; and bitterness, doubt; and doubt, despair
opt2: Tribulation worketh wealth; and wealth, power; and power, dominion
opt3: Tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope
opt4: Tribulation worketh wrath; and wrath, judgment; and judgment, fear
correct: Tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope
explanation: God uses trials to forge mature endurance, proven character (experience), and triumphant hope. Romans 5:3-4 (KJV) - "And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope:"

question: Why does Christian hope never disappoint or make ashamed according to Romans 5:5?
opt1: Because believers are guaranteed earthly fame and worldly prosperity
opt2: Because the angels constantly recite our names before the throne
opt3: Because the Roman Empire hath promised legal protection to the church
opt4: Because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us
correct: Because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us
explanation: The Holy Spirit floods the believer's inner heart with the experiential certainty of God's love. Romans 5:5 (KJV) - "And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us."

question: For whom did Christ die when we were yet without strength in Romans 5:6?
opt1: In due time Christ died for the ungodly
opt2: Christ died exclusively for the righteous and noble
opt3: Christ died only for those who kept the whole Law
opt4: Christ died for those who offered daily temple sacrifices
correct: In due time Christ died for the ungodly
explanation: Christ's death occurred at the divinely ordained moment for helpless, ungodly sinners. Romans 5:6 (KJV) - "For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly."

question: How does God uniquely demonstrate and commend His own love toward us in Romans 5:8?
opt1: By granting our ancestors rich harvests in the land of Canaan
opt2: In that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us
opt3: By overthrowing the pagan kingdoms of Greece and Rome
opt4: By establishing the temple of Solomon in golden splendor
correct: In that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us
explanation: Divine love is demonstrated beyond comparison because Christ died for rebels while they were still sinners. Romans 5:8 (KJV) - "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."

question: From what are believers much more guaranteed to be saved, having been justified by Christ's blood in Romans 5:9?
opt1: We shall be saved from all physical bodily illnesses in this life
opt2: We shall be saved from having to pay imperial Roman tribute
opt3: We shall be saved from wrath through him
opt4: We shall be saved from the malice of human enemies
correct: We shall be saved from wrath through him
explanation: Justification by Christ's blood provides absolute certainty of rescue from future eschatological wrath. Romans 5:9 (KJV) - "Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him."

question: How did sin and death enter into the human race according to Romans 5:12?
opt1: Through the disobedience of the angels who fell before creation
opt2: Through the building of the tower of Babel on the plain of Shinar
opt3: Through the worship of the golden calf in the wilderness of Sinai
opt4: By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned
correct: By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned
explanation: Adam's original transgression plunged all humanity into sin and universal physical and spiritual death. Romans 5:12 (KJV) - "Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:"

question: What magnificent contrast is established between Adam's offence and the gift of grace in Christ in Romans 5:17?
opt1: They which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ
opt2: Adam's sin was permanent and could never be reversed by divine grace
opt3: Only the direct descendants of David can overcome the curse of Adam
opt4: Grace restoreth man only to the garden of Eden on this present earth
correct: They which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ
explanation: Christ's gift of righteousness superabundantly reverses Adam's curse, causing believers to reign in life. Romans 5:17 (KJV) - "For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)"

question: What happens when sin abounds under the Law according to the triumphant axiom of Romans 5:20?
opt1: God's patience is exhausted and creation is immediately dissolved
opt2: Where sin abounded, grace did much more abound
opt3: The Law is amended to allow greater license to human weakness
opt4: The promises to the fathers are revoked for all future generations
correct: Where sin abounded, grace did much more abound
explanation: No matter how deeply human sin multiplies, God's superabounding grace infinitely surpasses and overcomes it. Romans 5:20 (KJV) - "Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:"

question: What indignant refutation does Paul give to the antinomian question: 'Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?'
opt1: Yes, for greater sin brings greater glory to the mercy of God
opt2: Only until the return of Christ to Jerusalem
opt3: God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?
opt4: The Law permitteth occasional sin if offerings are brought
correct: God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?
explanation: Believers have decisively died to sin's realm and power; continuing in deliberate sin is a moral impossibility. Romans 6:1-2 (KJV) - "What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?"

question: What spiritual reality is symbolized by Christian baptism into Jesus Christ in Romans 6:3-4?
opt1: A ceremonial washing qualifying believers to enter the temple courts
opt2: An initiation into an esoteric mystery cult of the Roman Empire
opt3: A physical sign replacing the circumcision of the flesh in the synagogue
opt4: Buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead, even so we also should walk in newness of life
correct: Buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead, even so we also should walk in newness of life
explanation: Baptism dramatizes the believer's co-burial and co-resurrection with Christ to walk in dynamic newness of life. Romans 6:4 (KJV) - "Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life."

question: What happened to our old man at the cross according to Romans 6:6?
opt1: Our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin
opt2: Our old man was reformed by education and rigorous moral discipline
opt3: Our old man was hidden in secret until the final day of judgment
opt4: Our old man was excused from punishment due to human frailty
correct: Our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin
explanation: The former unregenerate self was judicially executed with Christ, breaking the enslaving power of sin. Romans 6:6 (KJV) - "Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin."

question: What truth regarding Christ's resurrection guarantees the believer's permanent victory in Romans 6:9?
opt1: Christ must die again at the end of every age to renew the world
opt2: Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him
opt3: Death still holds power over Christ's earthly body until the kingdom
opt4: Christ dieth annually during the days of Unleavened Bread
correct: Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him
explanation: Christ's resurrection is definitive and permanent; death's dominion was broken forever. Romans 6:9 (KJV) - "Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him."

question: How does Paul command believers to reckon themselves in Romans 6:11?
opt1: Sinless in flesh, incapable of committing any moral mistake
opt2: Still under the condemning bondage of Moses' written law
opt3: Dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord
opt4: Independent sovereigns who answer to no divine authority
correct: Dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord
explanation: Faith counts (reckons) as true what God has accomplished: dead to sin's rule, vibrant and alive to God. Romans 6:11 (KJV) - "Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord."

question: Why shall sin not have dominion over believers according to the liberating promise of Romans 6:14?
opt1: Because believers are physically incapable of committing sin
opt2: Because an iron wall protects believers from demonic influence
opt3: Because the civil authorities enforce Christian morality by the sword
opt4: For ye are not under the law, but under grace
correct: For ye are not under the law, but under grace
explanation: Freedom from the Law's condemnation and transfer into the reign of grace shatters sin's tyrannical mastery. Romans 6:14 (KJV) - "For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace."

question: What universal principle of spiritual servitude is articulated in Romans 6:16?
opt1: To whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness
opt2: Every man is born naturally free and can never be enslaved spiritually
opt3: Spiritual servitude is determined solely by the stars and constellations
opt4: Only those who commit murder are truly enslaved to sin
correct: To whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness
explanation: Obedience reveals ultimate mastership: yielding to sin yields death; yielding to God yields righteousness. Romans 6:16 (KJV) - "Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?"

question: What blessed status do believers enjoy having been emancipated from sin in Romans 6:18?
opt1: Ye became earthly kings with authority over the nations
opt2: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness
opt3: Ye were permitted to indulge every appetite of the flesh without guilt
opt4: Ye were released from all accountability to civil government
correct: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness
explanation: True biblical freedom is not lawless autonomy, but liberation from sin into joyful enslavement to righteousness. Romans 6:18 (KJV) - "Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness."

question: What present fruit and ultimate end do servants of God possess according to Romans 6:22?
opt1: Ye have fruit unto worldly honor, and the end temporal wealth
opt2: Ye have fruit unto political mastery, and the end military triumph
opt3: Ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life
opt4: Ye have fruit unto ascetic mortification, and the end oblivion
correct: Ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life
explanation: Sanctification in progressive holiness is the organic fruit that culminates in eternal life. Romans 6:22 (KJV) - "But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life."

question: What stark, immortal contrast concludes Romans 6 in verse 23?
opt1: For the reward of virtue is earthly praise; but the cost of folly is poverty
opt2: For the law of Moses is eternal life; but the neglect of circumcision is death
opt3: For sin is repaid by temporal fines; but righteousness by golden crowns
opt4: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord
correct: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord
explanation: Sin pays its earned wages—eternal death; God freely bestows His unearned gift—eternal life in Christ. Romans 6:23 (KJV) - "For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord."

question: What marital analogy does Paul use in Romans 7:2-3 to explain the believer's release from the Law?
opt1: The woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed
opt2: A servant who buyeth his freedom with silver is no longer subject to his master
opt3: A soldier who completeth his service in the legion is exempt from military commands
opt4: A son who reacheth thirty years of age is no longer under his father's household
correct: The woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed
explanation: Just as death dissolves the marriage covenant legally, the believer's death with Christ severs the Law's claim. Romans 7:2 (KJV) - "For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband."

question: To whom are believers married now that they have become dead to the Law through Christ's body in Romans 7:4?
opt1: To the priesthood of Aaron, to offer unceasing incense in the holy place
opt2: That ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God
opt3: To the angelic watchers who govern the celestial spheres
opt4: To the restored commonwealth of Israel under the Davidic covenant
correct: That ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God
explanation: Believers are united to the risen Christ in an indissoluble spiritual union to bear righteous fruit for God. Romans 7:4 (KJV) - "Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God."

question: Which specific tenth commandment exposed Paul's inward covetousness and revealed the nature of sin in Romans 7:7?
opt1: Thou shalt not steal
opt2: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy
opt3: Thou shalt not covet
opt4: Honour thy father and thy mother
correct: Thou shalt not covet
explanation: The tenth commandment penetrates beneath outward actions to expose inward sinful desires (concupiscence). Romans 7:7 (KJV) - "What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet."

question: What happened to sin when the commandment came into Paul's consciousness in Romans 7:9?
opt1: Sin was immediately eradicated from his mortal flesh
opt2: Sin was restrained and rendered powerless to tempt him
opt3: Sin departed from him and entered into the uncircumcised
opt4: When the commandment came, sin revived, and I died
correct: When the commandment came, sin revived, and I died
explanation: The holy commandment provoked dormant sin into active rebellion, crushing Paul's legal self-righteousness. Romans 7:9 (KJV) - "For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died."

question: How does Paul vindicate the divine character of the Law in Romans 7:12?
opt1: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good
opt2: The Law was an imperfect ordinance given by angels that should be despised
opt3: The Law is carnal, corrupt, and the direct cause of human depravity
opt4: The Law is an outdated Jewish superstition without moral value
correct: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good
explanation: The fault lies not in the Law, which is intrinsically holy, just, and good, but in fallen human nature. Romans 7:12 (KJV) - "Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good."

question: What sharp contrast does Paul draw between the nature of the Law and his unredeemed flesh in Romans 7:14?
opt1: The law is weak and flawed, but the human spirit is pure and divine
opt2: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin
opt3: The law is binding only upon the body, but the soul is untouched
opt4: The law was written for angels, while man is governed by instinct
correct: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin
explanation: The Law reflects God's spiritual perfection, exposing man's fallen flesh as enslaved under sin. Romans 7:14 (KJV) - "For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin."

question: What humbling confession regarding the flesh does Paul record in Romans 7:18?
opt1: In my flesh resideth a spark of uncreated divine light
opt2: My flesh is naturally inclined toward all righteousness and truth
opt3: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing
opt4: My flesh hath been fully glorified since the day of my baptism
correct: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing
explanation: Apart from divine grace, the fallen human nature is devoid of any inherent spiritual goodness. Romans 7:18 (KJV) - "For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not."

question: What agonized moral paralysis does Paul describe regarding his daily performance in Romans 7:19?
opt1: I accomplish all righteous deeds easily without any inward struggle
opt2: I never desire to do good, but delight only in iniquity continually
opt3: The Law hath removed every desire to commit transgression from my heart
opt4: For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do
correct: For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do
explanation: Paul articulates the intense civil war between the regenerate desire for good and indwelling fleshly weakness. Romans 7:19 (KJV) - "For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do."

question: Where does the believer find true delight according to the inward man in Romans 7:22?
opt1: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man
opt2: In the philosophical academies of Athens and Alexandria
opt3: In the worldly praise and honors bestowed by the Sanhedrin
opt4: In the physical pleasures and appetites of the mortal body
correct: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man
explanation: The renewed inward man genuinely loves, cherishes, and delights in God's holy Law. Romans 7:22 (KJV) - "For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:"

question: What triumphant answer does Paul shout in reply to his cry: 'O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me' in Romans 7:24-25?
opt1: I shall deliver myself by my own willpower and fasting
opt2: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord
opt3: The high priest shall make atonement with the blood of bulls
opt4: The philosophical contemplation of virtue shall liberate my soul
correct: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord
explanation: Deliverance from the body of death comes not through self-effort or the Law, but solely through Jesus Christ. Romans 7:24-25 (KJV) - "O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin."

question: What monumental declaration of absolute security opens Romans chapter 8 in verse 1?
opt1: There is now temporary probation for those who keep the Sabbath
opt2: There is severe judgment reserved for every past transgression
opt3: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus
opt4: There is partial pardon granted to those who fast thrice a week
correct: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus
explanation: Union with Christ removes all judicial condemnation forever; believers stand completely acquitted. Romans 8:1 (KJV) - "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit."

question: What divine dynamic has liberated the believer from the tyranny of sin and death in Romans 8:2?
opt1: The decree of the Roman Senate granting religious toleration
opt2: The strict observance of the ceremonial ordinances of Moses
opt3: The natural moral development of the human intellect
opt4: The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death
correct: The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death
explanation: The life-giving power of the Holy Spirit overcomes the downward gravitational pull of sin and death. Romans 8:2 (KJV) - "For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death."

question: What is the spiritual consequence of carnality versus spiritual-mindedness in Romans 8:6?
opt1: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace
opt2: To be carnally minded is temporal poverty; but spiritually minded is earthly wealth
opt3: Both minds are equal in the sight of God if one is sincere
opt4: The carnal mind can be sanctified by animal sacrifices in the temple
correct: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace
explanation: A mind set on the flesh produces spiritual death, while a mind governed by the Spirit enjoys life and peace. Romans 8:6 (KJV) - "For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace."

question: Who are defined as the true sons of God in Romans 8:14?
opt1: Those who can trace their genealogy directly to Abraham and Isaac
opt2: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God
opt3: Those who hold office as priests and levites in the sanctuary
opt4: All who have been born into the Roman Empire as free citizens
correct: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God
explanation: The authentic badge of divine sonship is being actively led and sanctified by the Holy Spirit. Romans 8:14 (KJV) - "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."

question: What intimate filial cry do believers utter through the Spirit of adoption in Romans 8:15?
opt1: Elohim, Judge
opt2: Adonai, King
opt3: Abba, Father
opt4: Jehovah, Lord of Hosts
correct: Abba, Father
explanation: The Spirit replaces servile fear with the warm, affectionate intimacy of an adopted child crying 'Abba, Father'. Romans 8:15 (KJV) - "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father."

question: With whom does the Holy Spirit bear witness concerning our divine identity in Romans 8:16-17?
opt1: The Spirit beareth witness before Caesar that we are loyal subjects
opt2: The Spirit beareth witness to the Sanhedrin that we keep the feast days
opt3: The Spirit beareth witness with the angels that our works are flawless
opt4: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: and if children, then heirs
correct: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: and if children, then heirs
explanation: The Holy Spirit provides inward supernatural assurance that we are children of God and joint-heirs with Christ. Romans 8:16-17 (KJV) - "The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together."

question: How does Paul evaluate the afflictions of this present earthly life compared to future glory in Romans 8:18?
opt1: The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us
opt2: Present sufferings completely outweigh any future hope of heavenly reward
opt3: Present sufferings are signs that God has abandoned His church to the world
opt4: Present sufferings can be avoided by offering gold to the civil governors
correct: The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us
explanation: Present tribulations shrink into insignificance when weighed against the transcendent eternal weight of glory. Romans 8:18 (KJV) - "For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us."

question: How does the Holy Spirit assist believers in their weakness and prayerlessness in Romans 8:26?
opt1: By dictating written prayers to be recited mechanically thrice daily
opt2: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered
opt3: By dispatching guardian angels to whisper earthly secrets
opt4: By eliminating the necessity of prayer for justified believers
correct: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered
explanation: In our ignorance and frailty, the Spirit intercedes within us with inexpressible, profound divine groaning. Romans 8:26 (KJV) - "Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered."

question: What universal promise of sovereign providential care is pledged in Romans 8:28?
opt1: Believers shall never experience physical bereavement or material loss
opt2: All earthly governments shall bow down to Christian ministers
opt3: All things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose
opt4: Every desire of the mortal heart shall be granted immediately
correct: All things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose
explanation: God orchestrates every event—both pleasant and painful—for the ultimate eternal good of His called people. Romans 8:28 (KJV) - "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose."

question: What triumphant title belongs to believers in all afflictions through Christ who loved us in Romans 8:37?
opt1: Helpless victims who must endure the cruel fate of the stars
opt2: Earthly conquerors who overthrow Caesar by the sword
opt3: Martyrs whose names are forgotten in the annals of history
opt4: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us
correct: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us
explanation: Believers are hyper-conquerors (hypernikōmen) through Christ's invincible, inseparable love. Romans 8:37 (KJV) - "Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us."

question: What intense pastoral anguish did Paul express concerning his Jewish kinsmen in Romans 9:2-3?
opt1: I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren
opt2: I rejoice that they are excluded from the covenant for their rejection of Jesus
opt3: I have ceased praying for them because their hearts are completely hardened
opt4: I have petitioned Caesar to banish all unbelieving Jews from the provinces
correct: I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren
explanation: Paul's Christlike agony for his brethren was so profound that he could wish himself cut off if it would save them. Romans 9:2-3 (KJV) - "That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh:"

question: What supreme theological climax crowns the eight privileges of Israel enumerated in Romans 9:4-5?
opt1: That they shall possess the gold of all nations in the millennium
opt2: Of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen
opt3: That Moses shall descend from heaven to rule their twelve tribes
opt4: That the temple in Jerusalem shall stand indestructible for ever
correct: Of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen
explanation: Paul affirms the supreme deity of Jesus Christ: born physically of Israel, yet 'over all, God blessed for ever.' Romans 9:5 (KJV) - "Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen."

question: How does Paul explain that God's covenant word has not failed despite widespread Jewish unbelief in Romans 9:6?
opt1: Because God transferred His covenant promises to the Roman legions
opt2: Because physical circumcision automatically secures eternal salvation
opt3: For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel
opt4: Because the angels have taken the place of the twelve tribes
correct: For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel
explanation: Physical descent from Jacob does not constitute true spiritual Israel; election is based on divine promise, not biology. Romans 9:6 (KJV) - "Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel:"

question: Which son of Abraham was designated as the sole vehicle of the covenant promise in Romans 9:7-8?
opt1: Ishmael, the firstborn son of Hagar the Egyptian
opt2: Midian, the son of Keturah Abraham's second wife
opt3: Eliezer of Damascus, the steward of his household
opt4: In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed
correct: In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed
explanation: God distinguished between natural seed (Ishmael) and supernatural promise (Isaac) to demonstrate sovereign election. Romans 9:7-8 (KJV) - "Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed."

question: When did God sovereignly choose Jacob over Esau according to Romans 9:11?
opt1: The children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand
opt2: After Esau despised his birthright and sold it for red pottage
opt3: When Jacob returned from Haran with twelve righteous sons
opt4: After Jacob wrestled with the angel at the brook Jabbok
correct: The children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand
explanation: God's election operates prior to birth and independent of human works, resting entirely on His sovereign purpose. Romans 9:11 (KJV) - "(For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;)"

question: What divine prerogative did God declare unto Moses in Exodus 33:19, cited in Romans 9:15?
opt1: I will save all who offer sacrifices upon the brazen altar
opt2: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion
opt3: I will bless only those who keep all ten commandments
opt4: I will pardon any nation that buildeth a sanctuary in the desert
correct: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion
explanation: Mercy is not a debt owed to human merit, but a sovereign gift bestowed according to God's free goodwill. Romans 9:15 (KJV) - "For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion."

question: For what divine purpose did God raise up Pharaoh of Egypt according to Romans 9:17?
opt1: That he might build the pyramids as an eternal memorial of Egypt
opt2: That he might teach the children of Israel the arts of agriculture
opt3: That I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth
opt4: That he might rule over the four corners of the ancient world
correct: That I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth
explanation: God utilized Pharaoh's stubborn rebellion as a platform to display His omnipotent power and publish His name worldwide. Romans 9:17 (KJV) - "For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth."

question: What striking metaphor does Paul employ in Romans 9:20-21 to silence human arrogance against divine sovereignty?
opt1: Shall the sheep instruct the shepherd where to lead the flock
opt2: Shall the silver coin demand why it was stamped with Caesar's image
opt3: Shall the soldier question the general upon the field of battle
opt4: Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay

Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?"

question: Which Old Testament prophet does Paul quote in Romans 9:25 to foretell the calling of the Gentiles?
opt1: I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved (Osee/Hosea)

question: Over what stumblingstone did Israel stumble while pursuing righteousness by the works of the Law in Romans 9:32-33?

question: What is Paul's fervent heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel in Romans 10:1?

question: What fatal flaw undermined Israel's religious zeal according to Romans 10:2-3?
opt1: They refused to offer daily morning and evening sacrifices

question: How does Romans 10:4 define Christ's relationship to the Law for every believer?
opt1: For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth

correct: For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth

question: How near is the word of faith which the apostles preached according to Romans 10:8?
opt1: Hidden across the great ocean in the islands of the west

explanation: The gospel does not require impossible ascents to heaven or descents to the deep; it is immediately accessible by faith. Romans 10:8 (KJV) - "But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;"

question: What two essential, inseparable elements bring salvation according to Romans 10:9?
opt1: Pay the temple tithe annually, and keep the seven feasts of Moses

explanation: Public confession of Jesus' absolute Lordship combined with heart-belief in His physical resurrection guarantees salvation. Romans 10:9 (KJV) - "That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved."

question: What universal promise from the prophet Joel does Paul proclaim in Romans 10:13?
opt1: Only the circumcision of the house of David shall inherit the kingdom

question: What prophetic citation from Isaiah 52:7 highlights the beauty of gospel messengers in Romans 10:15?
opt1: How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

Romans 10:15 (KJV) - "And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!"

question: According to the famous axiom of Romans 10:17, how does saving faith originate in the human heart?
opt1: Faith cometh by philosophical meditation upon the cosmos

question: Through whom did God warn that He would provoke Israel to jealousy by a foolish nation in Romans 10:19?

First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you."

question: How does God describe His enduring posture toward Israel through Isaiah in Romans 10:21?
opt1: I have completely forgotten their names from the book of life

question: What personal autobiographical proof does Paul provide to refute the claim that God has cast away His people in Romans 11:1?
opt1: For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin
opt2: I was born a prince in the royal court of Herod the Great

opt4: I am the chief scribe over the archives of the Sanhedrin
correct: For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin

question: How many faithful men did God reveal He had reserved to Himself who had not bowed the knee to Baal in Romans 11:4?
opt1: Twelve thousand from each tribe

correct: Seven thousand men

question: What preserves the present Jewish remnant according to Romans 11:5?
opt1: According to their strict adherence to the oral traditions
opt2: According to their military resistance against the Roman empire
opt3: According to the election of grace
opt4: According to the merits of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
correct: According to the election of grace
explanation: The surviving spiritual remnant of Jewish believers exists solely by sovereign, unmerited grace. Romans 11:5 (KJV) - "Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace."

question: What providential purpose was accomplished through Israel's temporary stumbling in Romans 11:11?
opt1: God abolished the Old Testament Scriptures permanently

opt4: Through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy
correct: Through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy
explanation: Israel's tragic rejection became the occasion for gospel riches to flood the Gentile world, ultimately provoking Israel. Romans 11:11 (KJV) - "I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy."

question: What agricultural metaphor does Paul use in Romans 11:17 to describe the inclusion of Gentile believers?
opt1: Thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree

opt4: Thou wert wheat sown among the tares by the angels of heaven
correct: Thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree
explanation: Gentiles are unnatural wild olive branches graciously grafted into the cultivated olive tree of Abrahamic promise. Romans 11:17 (KJV) - "And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree;"

question: What solemn warning does Paul give Gentile believers against arrogance toward the broken Jewish branches in Romans 11:20?
opt1: Boast loudly in the marketplace over their destruction

correct: Be not highminded, but fear

question: What dual aspects of God's character are juxtaposed in Romans 11:22?
opt1: Behold the silence and distance of God

question: How long will the partial hardening (blindness) of Israel endure according to Romans 11:25?

Romans 11:25 (KJV) - "For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in."

question: What immutable truth regarding God's election of Israel is stated in Romans 11:29?

correct: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance (irrevocable)
explanation: God's covenant commitments and electing callings are irrevocable; He never regrets or cancels His promises. Romans 11:29 (KJV) - "For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance."

question: What majestic trinitarian doxology concludes Paul's profound exposition of election in Romans 11:36?
opt1: Unto Caesar Nero be tribute and honour from all the provinces for ever

correct: For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen
explanation: All reality originates in God (of Him), is sustained by God (through Him), and culminates in God's glory (to Him). Romans 11:36 (KJV) - "For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen."

question: What consecrated lifestyle does Paul urge believers to present to God in Romans 12:1?
opt1: Present annual offerings of bullocks and rams upon the altar

opt4: Pay two drachmas daily to support the temple priests in Jerusalem

Romans 12:1 (KJV) - "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service."

question: How are Christians transformed rather than conforming to this present world in Romans 12:2?
opt1: By adopting the outward dress and speech of the Roman patricians

explanation: Spiritual transformation (metamorphosis) begins inwardly through the Spirit-empowered renewal of the mind. Romans 12:2 (KJV) - "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."

question: What rule of humble self-assessment does Paul prescribe for every member of the body in Romans 12:3?

opt4: To assume that spiritual authority is purchased with silver and gold

explanation: True humility thinks soberly, recognizing that all gifts and faith are measured out by God's sovereign grace. Romans 12:3 (KJV) - "For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith."

question: How does Paul describe the unity and diversity of the church in Romans 12:4-5?
opt1: We are independent sovereigns who have no obligation to one another

explanation: Believers form a single interdependent spiritual organism in Christ, each possessing distinct functions. Romans 12:4-5 (KJV) - "For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another."

question: What authentic standard must govern Christian love according to Romans 12:9?
opt1: Let love be shown only to those of our own household and tribe

opt3: Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good

explanation: Genuine love is free from hypocrisy, abhorring evil while tenaciously clinging to what is morally good. Romans 12:9 (KJV) - "Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good."

question: How should believers express mutual honor and affection in Romans 12:10?
opt1: Demand that others bow down and acknowledge our spiritual seniority

explanation: Christian brotherhood outdoes itself in showing mutual respect, eagerly giving precedence to others. Romans 12:10 (KJV) - "Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;"

question: What three spiritual postures are linked together in the Christian walk in Romans 12:12?
opt1: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer

explanation: Hope fuels joy, patience weathers tribulation, and unceasing prayer sustains spiritual vitality. Romans 12:12 (KJV) - "Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;"

question: What compassionate empathy is commanded of believers in Romans 12:15?
opt1: Envy those who prosper, and mock those who suffer affliction

opt3: Maintain cold indifference toward the emotional states of others
opt4: Rejoice only when your personal enemies are overthrown
correct: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep
explanation: True Christian community enters deeply and selflessly into both the joys and heartaches of others. Romans 12:15 (KJV) - "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep."

question: Why are believers forbidden from taking personal vengeance in Romans 12:19?
opt1: Because personal revenge is too expensive to execute in Roman courts

opt4: Because wickedness will naturally disappear without any judgment

explanation: Quoting Deuteronomy 32:35, Paul commands believers to yield all retribution to God's righteous tribunal. Romans 12:19 (KJV) - "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord."

question: How does a believer overcome evil according to the closing imperative of Romans 12:21?
opt1: Overcome evil with greater violence and ruthless retaliation

opt4: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good
correct: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good
explanation: The supreme Christian triumph is conquering hatred through active, radical, benevolent goodness. Romans 12:21 (KJV) - "Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good."

question: What universal command regarding civil government is established in Romans 13:1?
opt1: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God
opt2: Let believers overthrow every pagan governor and establish a theocracy
opt3: Let Christians refuse to submit to any magistrate who is unbaptized

correct: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God
explanation: Civil authority is a divine institution; all earthly rulers govern under God's sovereign ordination. Romans 13:1 (KJV) - "Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God."

question: What warning is issued to those who resist legitimate civil authority in Romans 13:2?

opt4: They are exempt from all divine judgment if their cause is political
correct: Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation
explanation: Rebellion against lawfully appointed civil order is rebellion against God's established decree. Romans 13:2 (KJV) - "Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation."

question: What title and weapon define the civil magistrate's God-given role in Romans 13:4?

question: For what two reasons must believers be subject to civil authorities according to Romans 13:5?

explanation: Christian submission is motivated not merely by fear of temporal punishment, but by inward moral conscience before God. Romans 13:5 (KJV) - "Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake."

question: What civic obligations are Christians commanded to render unto all according to Romans 13:7?

correct: Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour
explanation: Christians must punctually pay taxes, customs, respect, and honor to established civil authorities. Romans 13:7 (KJV) - "Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour."

question: What permanent debt should believers maintain toward one another according to Romans 13:8?
opt1: Borrow continually from one another without repaying the principal

opt4: Owe allegiance only to those who share our exact political beliefs
correct: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law
explanation: Love is a continuing spiritual debt that can never be fully discharged, fulfilling the whole Law. Romans 13:8 (KJV) - "Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law."

question: Into what single comprehensive commandment are the moral prohibitions of the Law briefly comprehended in Romans 13:9?

question: Why is love declared to be the fulfilling of the Law in Romans 13:10?

question: What eschatological urgency does Paul press upon the church in Romans 13:11-12?

explanation: The impending dawn of Christ's return demands spiritual vigilance and casting off works of darkness. The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light."

question: What positive command closes Romans 13 regarding personal holiness and the flesh in verse 14?
